text:
John Tavares came back from injury into the worst stretch of Toronto's season. The Leafs have lost every one of his last ten games, eight in regulation, and a Daily Faceoff Toronto post on Saturday put the losing streak at eight. The hometown captain-turned-alternate is now in headlines about uncertain futures, with Heavy.com running one claim under the words "Get Them Out of Here."

He has done his part lately, with goals in back-to-back games against Chicago and Los Angeles and 10 points in 15 games overall. The five-on-five picture is the hard part: Toronto has taken just 36% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. Our numbers say his team has also scored 6.1 fewer goals than those chances deserve, so some of the damage is bad luck, but the chances themselves have been poor.

The skill that made him a 500-goal scorer is still there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.1 scoring chances per 60 from the slot area in 2025-26, 98th percentile, and Evolving-Hockey noted he did it with weak linemates against top competition. At 36, he projects to 55 points by our numbers.
headline: Tavares is back, and the Leafs' slide is the story
